item.title: SCP Idea Whale Eating Bird
item.description: A giant bird that hunts whales, based off of the Thunderbird cryptid. My first attempt at an article.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: No, at least not yet.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre:I haven't settled on one yet, though it will likely be action/suspense.

Layout: Information presentation

Elevator Pitch: A Keter class giant bird, living on an island in the Pacific, hunting whales like an osprey. Unnaturally large and fast, it occasionally attacks human ships.

Central Narrative: The Foundation deploys operatives to the North Pacific after a large bird attacks a group of whale watchers. After some investigation, they are unable to find anything, but stay posted. A few years later, a surfaced Soviet Submarine is sunk by the creature. The Foundation ramps up the search, eventually tracking it to a remote island between Chile and New Zealand. A submarine is sent to drop off a scout crew, but the sub is sunk because they underestimate how deep the creature can dive. A cruiser is deployed, and fires upon the creature when it attempts to dive at it. The bird survives, but the mission is called off to avoid potentially killing it. Another sub is deployed, this time equipped with an improved diving system to get down faster, and more ships surrounding the area to track it by RADAR. The crew treks up the small dormant volcanic island, and finds a nest made of logs with scattered bones. When the RADAR team radios them to say that the bird is returning home, they quickly find that it is coming faster than expected, and the submarine that they arrived on is unable to pick them up. They are forced to spend a night on the island with the bird, but it barely acknowledges them. It is determined that the creature is not a threat, and will be contained simply by baiting it away from coasts and sea lanes.

Hook: The Special Containment Procedure stands out compared to the SCPs I've read. The bird itself isn't dangerous enough to warrant destruction, and generally isolates itself. The Foundation would figure that it's more worthwhile to monitor it, and keep the thing away from humans.

This is my first Article, so I'm a bit nervous about it. Also, I'm aware that there is already a "Thunderbird" Article, but the concept for this one is completely different.

item.title: SCP Proposal: The Red Girl (1st SCP)
item.description: A new humanoid, Euclid-class SCP, which undergoes some dangerous changes when exposed to rage, anger or frustration, to erase those feelings in a rather vicious way.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX, AKA the Red Girl, is a humanoid anomaly which takes the appearance of a 15-16 year old girl with with long hair and irises in a unnatural shade of bright red. The Red Girl shows usually sweet, affective behavior, but will get triggered if she gets visually or audibly exposed to rage or hatred, or senses rage in a nearby person. SCP-XXXX will undergo a rapid transformation, in which she grows red scales on 60% of her body, will grow claws and fangs and the hair will turn into spikes. SCP-XXXX will then attempt to viciously attack the person that it sensed the anger from, often resulting in a chain reaction if multiple people are nearby, although it will never attack more than 8 people in a row. After the attack, SCP-XXXX will show shock and remorse over its own deeds, and slowly regain her human appearance. Attempts learn SCP-XXXX to control this states have proven ineffective, as the Red Girl seems to lose all memories of the incident within the next 8 hours.

Central Narrative: Although the origins of the Red Girl are unknown, SCP-researchers have constructed several theories of why its attacks are aimed at people who carry negative feelings towards others: what if SCP-XXXX was created with the purpose of simply erasing all negative feelings in this world? Did the creator attempt to slowly rebuild a more positive and tolerant society? Or did they simply want to create a environment of fear and sadness for those who have committed the sin of wrath? The answer is still unknown, as SCP-XXXX doesn't seem to know herself about her creation and her memories of incidents continuously get erased.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that the mystery of her creation might become an interesting topic. Furthermore, I think the Red Girl fits the category of humanoid SCP's who have limited power over their anomalous abilities and actions, such as SCP-053, SCP-073 or SCP-2662, without being too similar to either of them. I also feel an SCP with something that resembles a dual personality disorder is a rather unused concept.

item.title: The Hungry Constellation
item.description: A shape-shifting constellation that can give anomalous properties to whatever it 'eats' based on a two-dimensional perspective from a specific observer
item.content:encoded:
The anomaly is a constellation that can take the shape of any Earth-like creature that has a mouth that can be displayed easily in two-dimensions from a perspective, say, a beak. The anomaly is inactive by default, but can be activated for a while if a selected group of people see it, a group which I haven't decided on yet. Once activated, the jaws or beaks or etc. of the constellation closes very slowly, and anything that is 'inside' the jaw relative to the observer from the group of people is destroyed.

In a nutshell, a constellation that gets hungry when a select observer from a group of people sees it.

item.title: The Sandman (GREENLIGHT WANTED)
item.description: "It dragged me into my nightmare where it wished for all to feed it's slumbering insanity." Entity based on the Ole Lukøje that connects a subject’s experience in their dream world to reality.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: A horrific humanoid that makes any person they encounter a narcoleptic, anyone affected by the humanoid will be stalked until they fall asleep which they will then enter the Sandman’s dreamscape where they are lured into a sense of security before being murdered and/or eaten alive gruesomely through mutilation. The subject of this encounter will be conscious the whole time while they’re unable to escape as it slowly eats and/or mutilates the subject. The victim is driven to insanity before the end of this encounter. When the victim awakens due to his unhinged state, they are a severe danger to everything around them.

Central Narrative: A husband comes home to find his wife and kids mutilated corpses on the floor. As he begins to cry, he falls to the floor to awaken in a dream state where he sees his wife sitting on a shorefront. He approaches her but as he gets close her head spins around revealing a disgusting face with a split jaw. Her limbs and skin start to turn into sand and fall off revealing something that so ugly and hideous he starts to puke. He can’t stop eventually starts to puke out blood trying to scream for help. It slowly approaches him and as it does the man stops puking only for his jaw to be ripped off and his frontal lobe to be crushed by the creature’s mouth where he is then eaten alive, completely conscious throughout the whole experience. He wakes up next to his dead family and he is extremely over joyous. He starts kicking over furniture and jumping on his deceased family’s corpses while cackling. He stomps his infant’s corpse to a pulp and exclaims, “This is the best day of m,” before he is cut off as his jaw shoots off, a big portion of his frontal lobe vanishing instantly, his ribcage snapping open to reveal nothing inside. Before he even hits, he is already dead. The creature is satisfied as he looks down on the dead family, it looks out the window to see more flesh to be devoured and the cycle starts again.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Entity based on the Ole Lukøje that connects a subject’s experience in their dream world to reality. "It dragged me into my nightmare where it wished for all to feed its slumbering insanity."

Additional Notes: Feedback on the hook if anything.

item.title: They Just Keep Searching
item.description: Seeking critique and possible greenlights for my first SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I posted this one before, but that was well over two weeks ago and it didn't get any responses. Figured I might as well try this forum again before looking into other critique options :) (I have made some very slight modifications since, anyway).

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make heavy use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 10 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Eventually these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and high resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Will search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP idea so I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away! I'm still trying to think of a better name for it.

item.title: Tower of Babel (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.description: An idea I had.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Occurs over several iterations, with the threat increasing over time

+ View Block
- Hide

Elevator Pitch: - A memetic effect which can be transferred through print, speech, or digital media.

-The infection causes all infected individuals to begin speaking in an info-hazardous language. Every 2 days infected individuals will become paralysed for an increasing period of time. Within 7 months this paralysis will become permanent.

-Individuals affected by the anomaly will be conscious during the period of paralysis, being somehow disconnected from their body and walking around in an incorporeal form. Within this form, they will be unable to communicate with any other affected individuals or non-affected individuals. When in this form, a massive black obelisk, which called Iskententhine (translating to 'That which is the end)

-Affected individuals are unaware of the memetic basis of their infection unless told, and as such are likely to speak to everyone as if speaking in normal English.

Central Narrative: -Anomaly is first thought to be safe, as an anomaly affecting the population of a factory near a city that doesn't exist (this is important), but soon is reclassified as Euclid as several foundation researchers and D-Class are infected (The Euclid level object is a new iteration). The foundation researchers are amneticised [[footnote]] This is spelled wrong]] and contained, but it is believed that one infection gets out, as the infection reappears in the high school where a researchers son lives.

-Object is re-classified as Keter after the infection is thought to be neutralised by aggressive foundation action, and efforts to bury all affected individuals. The effect re-appears in several different locations following this, and soon large swaths of humanity are infected. Several prominent foundation members move into secure facilities to wait out the disaster. SCP-2000 is activated, the foundation recommends suicide for all individuals and efforts from several Groups of interests create a 1km layer of dirt and dust over the original earth, creating new geological formations. Shortly after, the O5 leave the containment chamber, recreate humanity, and continue.

The final iterations object class is Cernunnos, and it seems that the infection has arisen again, in Site 102, Canberra, Australia.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Will the foundation sacrifice human communication permanently to save humanity?

Notes: I had a wildly different idea under the same name previously. This article is completely different from that (the only thing in common is the hook), so I've put it in a new thread.

item.title: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.description: An anomalous and dangerous creature lurks in the depths of the Atlantic,
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is large, dark, quadrupedal aquatic lifeform located somewhere in the Atlantic at a site known as The Ring. SCP can only viewed at night at designated platforms 350m below sea level. Videoing or photographing SCP-XXXX must be avoided as well as viewing it for more than 1 minute continuously, or making direct eye contact.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX was first alerted to the SCP foundation through a field agent located inside of NOAA. NOAA identified a drastic change in salinity in an area roughly 1km2 somewhere in the Atlantic. Field Agents Smith, Jones, Roger, Greeves and Alex investigated the site of this anomalous activity using a SCP ship Horizon. Upon arrival the agents confirmed a change in salinity within the area as well as mutated and aggressive versions of the local fauna and flora. All agents sent to investigate this anomalous area during this initial Expedition, never returned. The last contact with the foundation in the transcript logs ended with the lead agent Smith saying:

"It's in the water, its in my head, its on the boat… send Deep Feeders"
After a considerable loss of life and 3 more expeditions were the foundation able to secure SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is capable Phycological Physical Mutation creating a sub entity of various forms like the Gespenst( wraith). SCP is also capable of salinity conversion, which if left uncheck can cause cataclysmic change in weather, flora/fauna, disrupt oxygen levels.

Additional Notes:Constructive criticism is greatly appreciated.👍

item.title: The Painter (Old Concept)
item.description: He is the judge that shall decide the fate of humans, you cannot escape your own fate.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror.

Elevator Pitch: The Painter is a faceless humanoid male with little to no facial features, the exception being it's eyes, it is able to decide the (horrible and gruesome) fate of any living human by painting it on a canvas (fate as in the way they die). No matter how hard it's victims will try they will always meet their fate, this manipulates the world around the victim so that they will meet their fate no matter the cost, it's only limitation is that it must know how the victim looks like in order to put them on a canvas. The foundation is unable to take the paintbrush and the canvas of the Painter because it's own fate is to keep painting until the end of mankind itself, so any attempt in doing so will result in an inevitable failure because there will always be a series of unstoppable events that will result in the painter getting it's necessary tools for it to continue painting.

Central Narrative: The Painter's story is that it is the judge of humanity, it is here to create and manipulate everyone's fate, it decides how and when everyone will experience their final moments and it will not stop until everyone's fate is set. The foundation also needs to severely restrict the painter's knowledge of any other SCPs, just imagine the damage if it were to paint a scientist in the jaws of 682, a huge containment breach would have to happen in order for the scientist to meet their fate.

The Painter was originally found in a cabin in the woods after a few campers reported "a weird man painting them dying in horrible ways". After a few years all of the campers died exactly how they reported the paintings to look like and that's when the foundation stepped in, they used smoke grenades, thermal vision and a bag to blind the target and capture it, but being captured by the foundation was only part of it's fate, it will use the foundation's infinite resources in order to keep painting.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The article will contain a few of the many victims of the Painter and how they met their grim fate, how the foundation will conduct tests on the painter and how it's anomalous world manipulation effect had a change on the world and the foundation.

Additional Notes: This is an old idea, my first one actually, I made an old thread about it almost a year ago and I'm trying to revisit the concept and improve it. hopefully I will be able to achieve that, if you decide to visit the old thread and find that you like the original concept more or some ideas from it, just let me know.

item.title: "Long" Beach California (Seeking Greenlights)
item.description: Anomalous section of California coastline
item.content:encoded:
Anomalous section of California coastline which demonstrates non-euclidean terrain, as you can walk all you want and never get any closer to the water, which appears to be only 90-ish yards away. It gets a little more interesting, trust me.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): N/A

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article. Name, Classification, Containment procedures, description.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a beach sixty miles south of Long Beach, California upon which, no matter how long an individual walks across the beach, the water can never be reached. However, the water always appears to be no more than eighty to ninety yards away. The actual anomaly is slightly more interesting than that, as you'll see in the central narrative below.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Through a series of audio logs between expeditionary personnel and command, as well as autopsy reports, readers will follow teams of research personnel sent to explore SCP-XXXX in hopes to discover more about its anomalous nature. The first expeditionary log reveals that the team suffers a casualty by "dry-drowning" around eight km out, and the others are recovered. Autopsy reveals cause of death to be asphyxia by drowning. The second log reveals that the use of a SCBA allows explorers to venture out substantially farther, reaching close to twenty six kilometers before their oxygen tanks reach half-way empty and they have to turn around. The third log follows a team of researchers more well equipped, with oxygen tanks that should last forty-eight hours. The team reports back around fifty-three km out that there is some form of writing in the sand. Later, they report that they can see what they believe to be a boat in the distance, just off shore, however at the fifty-seven km mark three of the five oxygen tanks simultaneously malfunction. The team turns around, holding their breath unless breathing in through the SCBA, which they take turns using to survive. All team members are recovered, and the writing in the sand is sent to linguists for deciphering. Log four, the final log before SCP-XXXX is deemed unfit for exploration, documents the exploration of four research personnel on board a semi-aquatic vehicle designed to withstand high pressure and impact. They make it twenty-six km before the vehicle begins to flood with water. The team is forced to abandon the vehicle and carry on. At the fifty-seven km mark, the lead researcher calls in that there appears to be a tall, disproportionate figure down near the water, henceforth denoted as SCP-XXXX-1. Before command gets a chance to respond, all personnel experience simultaneous SCBA failures, and the hissing of air and screaming of researchers can be heard just before comm connection is lost. Three of the four corpses are recovered and autopsied, and cause of death is determined to be asphyxia by drowning. The fourth cable comes back severed, and there is blood and a torn shred of clothing on the cable.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A beach that kills people by "dry drowning" them is certainly unique. The test logs will serve as something to actually keep readers interested.

Additional Notes: Researchers in the audio logs are tethered by spools of cable so they can be recovered. All feedback still welcome.

I have attached a draft of an audio log (albeit not a great one, it is still a draft) for posterity

item.title: The No-Tell Motel
item.description: A seemingly unassuming roadside Motel in the Mojave Desert is actually a fixed point that exist in multiple realities.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, (Some) Comedy, Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): Article Format

Elevator Pitch:

  • A seemingly unassuming small hotel in the Mojave Desert
  • The interior is infinitely larger than the exterior
  • The motel is a fixed point in multiple realities
  • There's no observable staff from outside
  • Those who have seen the staff cannot recall any personal features, only that they are polite and courteous
  • Those who stay past check out are escorted out by security, also whose features are unable to be recalled
  • The halls are infinite and labyrinthine
  • The motel rooms are generic and normal-seeming
  • The motel room windows each look out on different worlds
  • Some people who leave the motel are from alternate Earths
  • Despite the monitoring and security, somehow, sometimes some people manage to get past to check in

Central Narrative: World-building

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The motel occasionally has a guest who stays in a room that looks out onto our world, and the dressers are filled with money from different time periods and countries, some of which no longer exist or have never existed. And the money includes ancient drachmas, crudely carved red painted stones, and etc.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure where I need help, but I gladly accept any advice willing to be given! (Also, I want to write a story about this SCP. Do I need to submit a separate thread?)

item.title: SCP-5158
item.content:encoded:
It looks like the boundless night sky, stars twinkling in droves.

item.title: One More Week
item.description: A backpack that allows its owner to live for one week, but at the cost of someone else's life.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Urban Legend

Page Layout: Standard description, some interview

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a beaten backpack with UC, Santa Cruz, patches on it. Once opened the person opening it is slowly replaced, physically and mentally, with a young philosophy student who then returns to exploring the continental United States. He also writes about his experiences, which helps pay his way.

Central Narrative: In 1989 Charles Anton Page decided to drop out of college and explore America; he felt trapped and needed to run away. He quickly adopted a "one week at a time" philosophy, where he'd find odd jobs and beg in order to obtain enough to buy a bus ticket and some food, and then would take off on the next leg of his journey.

A year or so later, he was robbed and left for dead, and would eventually succumb to his wounds. The body was never recovered. His backpack, and the contents therein, were pawned at a local pawn shop. Someone bought the backpack, and over the next few hours was transformed into a virtual clone of Page, but without the knowledge of his death or that he was leading an extended life.

He is able to live for one week (168 hours) at a time before copies of the wounds that killed him appear on his body, and he then quickly succumbs to them. Once someone finds and opens the backpack, he is yet again allowed to live for another week, but with the usual memory lapse.

While he has adapted to the modern world somewhat (he writes a blog instead of magazine articles), he is still driven to explore the continental United States. He just does it one week at a time.

Hook/Attention Grabber: A basic urban legend about a youth cut short but still trying to find a way to accomplish his dream of exploring the United States through a mix of odd jobs, bus tickets, and hitchhiking, one week at a time.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Comedy, Weirdness, short and sweet

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation stumbles upon a small family-owned restaurant that happens to serve infallibly, undeniably good food.

Central Narrative: After being flagged by CHORUS, A social mapping AIC designed to detect intense spikes in mood, a small pizzeria finds itself under the attention of the Foundation. The restaurant, known as Giacomo's Pizza, makes the pretty standard claim that it serves "The World's Best." The thing is, for this bistro, that might actually be true. Anyone who tries Giacomo's pies agrees that they're the best they ever tasted -or will taste- to the point of profound satisfaction. The thing is, the foundation can't figure out why. It's just normal pizza; nothing memetic, nothing thaumaturgic, nothing chemical. In the end, when the lead researcher breaks down to the current Giacomo in charge, tearfully asking them what's so special about their pizza they merely reply "Simple. They're made with love."
Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook of the article lies in the surrealist concept of an item of food being objectively "the best." As well as the intrigue of the eyecatching associated image:

item.title: Tale 1 of Tau-13
item.description: First tale detailing the missions of (my) MTF unit Tau-13
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre(s): Horror, Action

Page Layout: Given that this is a tale, I was going to write it like your standard narrative-driven novel. This is also the format I write most things in, save aspects of the SCP article I've drafted.

Elevator Pitch:

  • This first one will detail the team's first mission together, with flashbacks to their lives together in training.
  • The mission will involve them investigating a cult-like organization (Sarkicism), who have been reportedly been kidnapping locals from a nearby town.
  • Upon investigation, they learn that it's all being done by the Sarkicists, and that most kidnapped locals are being used as sacrifices to try and summon some horrible Lovecraftian creature. The Sarkicists succeed at this, making it all the more urgent.
  • They, of course, go in for expulsion and containment.
  • They have a hard-fought battle, and through some stupid, neglectful mistakes, they lose their private to the monster.
  • Since they had all grown together in training and just as good friends, the sight of their private getting killed, combined with the psychic effects of the monstrosity, drive them very near to the edge of insanity.
  • After eventually routing out the cult, they return with broken minds. I'm thinking I'll have the Foundation use amnestics to make them forget the horrors, but deep down they still have that vastly stronger, Pavlovian-esque drive to protect each other and all innocents from these, and similar, horrors1.

item.description: [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
New to the site and looking to get this concept critiqued and, hopefully, greenlit.

Thread summary moved to the main post as the thread is now locked.

The idea is for an SCP that is a roadside motel in the Arizona desert. This motel is a fixed point in multiple realities. The different worlds can be viewed from the different room's windows. The inside is infinitely bigger inside than outside, and labyrinthine. Examples include a barren white world of perpetual night, at the bottom of an alien ocean, an alien swamp, and etc. Creatures and other entities can break through the windows from time to time. There appears to be no staff, until those who are drawn to enter it "check out" the next day. The staffs' features can never be remembered by those that observe them. It is Euclid class, and fenced off with posted guards. Yet, still, sometimes civilians and even a guard or two, somehow, manage to enter.

item.title: "Now thats what I call existence"
item.description: A CD that transports listeners to a otherworldly collection.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy, Existential Happiness

Elevator Pitch: An unmarked CD that can transport any listener to a seemingly infinite hall like room. The room is covered in forms of digital media, every piece being some form of strange variation of the cd "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!".

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: SCP researchers and class D personal are transported to the collection room and are greeted by a sign that hangs off of a rail attached to the ceiling of this room that spans the full length. The sign moves into view, all that is said on the sign is "Welcome, and enjoy my collection." The Article will be split into two parts mainly, with the researchers walking down the hall and noting interesting deviations with certain items in the collection. Examples include "That's what I call actor Andy Warhol's face Vol 1!" and "That's what I call just Hoobastank Vol 1!".

The second section would detail the research teams further dives into the hall. After multiple hours of walking they come to another sign hanging from a rail, this sign precedes more of the hall but every shelf past this sign is empty. The sign proclaims that the rest of the hall is dedicated to alternate universe versions of earth that have not yet made their respective version of "That's what I call music Vol 1!". The sign then begins to wax poetic about how no matter the horrific world or terrifying problems humanity may fall under, almost every single version of humanity has had it in them to at *least* make one version of "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!". The collection is a testament to humanities capacity to at least make this one cd every time.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The foundation never actually sees the being behind the collection, and Nothing actually dangerous happens to the researchers, its just a strange walk through a weird "turtles all the way down" style museum

Additional Notes: This is my first real scp idea that I've put any weight into actually writing about and I made this post for the critique it needs but also just to make sure that this idea isn't something that has already been made. Thank you for reading

item.title: Axolotl
item.description: Earth’s guardian, taking the form of a massive axolotl, waiting to protect the Earth when the end of the world arrives
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A massive axolotl which lives in it’s own dimension outside of space-time . It’s regenerative abilities are so advanced, it's nearly immortal. When the end of the world comes, naturally, or in the form of an “XK end of the world scenario”, the entity will appear from its dimension to fight off the opposing force.

Central Narrative: The creature was first spotted very early in the foundation’s history. Its head was first seen coming through a wormhole leading back to its home, during one of the first XK class scenario breeches, nicknamed “Lil’ Devil”. Lil’ Devil’s body radiated immense heat, which caused drastic changes to the surrounding environment.Nearly seconds before the foundation planned to launch their final attack, the axolotl lunged from its wormhole, which it had previously moved very slowly threw, snapped at Lil’ Devil, got it in one fell swoop with no damage to the surrounding area or its self, and disappeared back threw the wormhole; leaving the foundations task force stunned. Throughout the foundation’s history, the wormhole has been spotted around the world, when the possibility of the end of the world is near, but the creature hasn’t been seen coming through the wormhole since that initial spotting, except for one education, where just the tip of the axolotls poked out of the worm hole, and completely demolished a nature reserve and multiple endangered birds in the process… That all happened after the opposing force was already naturalized. Research on the creature has been challenging because of how it never leaves its wormhole, however, they have found many carvings and paintings of the axolotl all around the world, dating back thousands of years. On multiple occasions researchers found carvings of it fighting off creatures assumed to be SCP-like entities. Some researchers think the axolotl acts out of love and fondness for humanity, having shown, despite its gigantic size, to have been very precise in how it ate Lil’ Devil, making sure any drastic movements wouldn't cause harm to civilians. Recently with more XK scenarios possible, the foundation has been hard at working on trying to make contact with the creature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I just think it’s kind of a fun and funny idea that the being which will protect Earth when the end of the world approaches, is a giant immortal axolotl, just waiting in its dimension for that time to come.

Central Narrative: The story is mostly told through historical documentation of an old Foundation site created post WWII. A former Obskurakorps base holding a part flesh and part mechanical entity that changes a area near it to that of another dimension. The Foundation spends years exploring these dimensions as the entity opens them though is never able to control the entity or understand how it works. It is revealed in an interview log with a captured scientist that the machine is searching for the Norse worlds of myth. Some it has found and others it continues to search for all while the potential threat of a hidden cell of the GOI remains at large.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The unknown factors that remain hidden and indecipherable all the while presenting a new threat to the foundation. The mystery that surrounds the site and the new worlds potentially within the Foundations grasp as well as the new twist it adds to a current GOI.

Additional Notes: I’d appreciate any feedback on tips to progress my article through the sites greenlighting process as this is still pretty new to me and I’d like to get it right.

item.title: A recursive Zip Archive.
item.description: A ZIP file that contains an exact copy of itself. This is a real thing.
item.content:encoded:
I don't know if real things qualify for SCP articles but there is this thing called a recursive zip file aka a "quine". Link here: https://research.swtch.com/zip

What makes this remind me of an anomalious SCP is the fact that when you open a quine zip file, you find an exact copy of itself inside. Extracting the contents will reveal an identical copy of the zip file you just extracted. Extracting that one will reveal yet another one. Round and round we go.

To make a more SCPish analogy, think of a box that contains another box the same size. And inside this box is another box of the same size as well. And so on and so forth.

So what we have is basically a zip file that seemingly pulls data out of thin air. The link contains example files to see for yourself.

What do you think?

item.title: A 4th degree burn
item.description: Ouch oof my nervous system
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Normal scp page layout

Elevator Pitch: Keter level scp, when humans sustain burns of incredibly high temperatures, their nervous systems re-wire to survive in intense heat. They turn into vaguely humanoid personages of flame who can't talk and can only live in intense heat.

Central Narrative: Instances of this scp are rare, due to level's of heat required to create this scp
rarely occur on earth. The narrative would follow the foundation containing several instances of this scp after a failed rocket launch in South Korea. After losing several instances due to decreasing temperatures, they are able to create a containment chamber with a increased temperature so then the final instance could be contained. Examination shows that a modified version of the nervous system is intact, and interviews show that the instances can "feel", as if they still had a body. Communicating is done through manipulating the flame into short words, although they describe this process as "Painful." The foundation can recreate this and they roast a D-class and make another instance. They then cool down the chamber and discover the temperature they "die" at.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: Similar to other skips, instances hate their predicament, but the foundation refuses to let them die so then they can contain the anomaly. The foundation in cold, y'all. Basically it's the fear of literally burning forever. A literal hell.

Additional Notes: I don't know the exact temperature the conversion takes place yet, i'll do some research later.
